name: known_divergences_catalog
description: Machine-readable catalog of ACCEPTED cross-SDK divergences - the allowlist the parity discipline checks against. Every entry must carry exactly the keys id, sdk, category, status, description, parity_scope, allowed_difference, tracking; status has exactly one legal value, 'intended' - a divergence that is not intended is a bug to fix, never a row to add. `sdk` names the SDK whose behavior differs from the shared contract ('ts' or 'py'). `parity_scope` states what MUST remain identical despite the divergence; `allowed_difference` states precisely what is permitted to differ - an entry whose allowed_difference would cover an enforcement-verdict difference is invalid by policy, not just by schema. Structure is validated by BOTH test suites (sdk/tests/unit/fixture-bookkeeping.test.ts, sdk-python/tests/test_fixture_bookkeeping.py), so a malformed or vocabulary-expanding entry fails CI in either language. The narrative History of fixed divergences stays in known-divergences.md - this catalog replaces only the live table.

categories.enforcement_surface: one SDK applies an identical verdict through a weaker or different mechanism
categories.evaluation_context: one SDK evaluates a rule with less context on some path
categories.dependency: a capability resolves through an optional dependency in one SDK
categories.capability: a control or emission exists in only one SDK today

entries.description: Customer policyRules eval context on the TS integration path: integrations/core.ts applyPreCallPolicy passes customer rules {provider, metadata} with no top-level model / currentEnvironment, so a customer model_gate / environment_gate rule is inert there, while the Python shared pre-call and the TS proxy wrapper source both. Enriching the context would newly fire previously-inert rules - a behavior change for existing users, out of scope for the additive floor slice.
entries.parity_scope: The anti-tamper FLOOR threads model + currentEnvironment on all paths in both SDKs (as of 2026-07-20); a rule promoted into policyFloor gates identically everywhere.
entries.allowed_difference: Customer (non-floor) model_gate / environment_gate rules do not fire on the TS integrations path.
entries.tracking: integrations/core.ts applyPreCallPolicy rules context. Revisit as its own slice with a migration note.

entries.description: Signed-policy verification backend: TypeScript verifies Ed25519 with node:crypto, always present. Python has no stdlib Ed25519, so policy_verify.py resolves an OPTIONAL backend (cryptography, then PyNaCl). With policy_public_key pinned and neither installed, Python reaches a state TypeScript cannot: it cannot check the signature at all. The package ships zero mandatory runtime dependencies, and the degraded state is declared rather than hidden.
entries.parity_scope: All shared signature vectors resolve to identical verdicts once a backend is installed (pip install "obsvr-sdk[crypto]", included in the dev extra so CI runs them for real); Python still fails closed without one - the fetched policy is refused, last-good stays in force, and policy_verification_unavailable is stamped into reserved metadata on every subsequent event.
entries.allowed_difference: The unverifiable-but-declared degraded state exists only in Python, only with a pinned key and no optional crypto backend.
entries.tracking: sdk-python/obsvr/policy_verify.py. Closes if a stdlib Ed25519 ever lands or the dependency posture changes.
